ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, a cup filled with water is placed tilted on a horizontal table surface. Its cross-section can be considered a rectangle with width $BC=6\, \text{cm}$ and length $CD=16\, \text{cm}$. When the water surface touches the edge of the cup, half of side $CD$ is above the water surface. What is the height of the water surface in centimeters at this moment?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $BF\perp AF$ at $F$, as shown in the diagram:\\
Since $BC=6$ cm, $CD=16$ cm, and $CE=\frac{1}{2}CD$,\\
Therefore $CE=8$ cm,\\
Since $\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
By the Pythagorean theorem, we have $BE=\sqrt{BC^{2}+CE^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{2}+8^{2}}=10$,\\
Since $\angle BCE=\angle FBE=90^\circ$,\\
Therefore $\angle EBC=\angle ABF$,\\
Since $\angle BCE=\angle BFA=90^\circ$,\\
Therefore $\triangle CBE\sim \triangle FBA$,\\
Therefore $\frac{BE}{AB}=\frac{BC}{BF}$,\\
i.e., $\frac{10}{16}=\frac{6}{BF}$,\\
Therefore $BF=\boxed{\frac{48}{5}}$.

Its cross-section can be considered a rectangle with width $BC=6\,\text{cm}$ and length $CD=16\,\text{cm}$. When the water surface touches the edge of the cup, half of side $CD$ is above the water surface. What is the height of the water surface in centimeters at this moment?

Construct $BF\perp AF$ at $F$, as shown in the diagram:\\
Since $BC=6$ cm, $CD=16$ cm, and $CE=\frac{1}{2}CD$,\\
Therefore $CE=8$ cm,\\
Since $\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
By the Pythagorean theorem, we have $BE=\sqrt{BC^{2}+CE^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{2}+8^{2}}=10$,\\
Since $\angle BCE=\angle FBE=90^\circ$,\\

Since $\angle BCE=\angle BFA=90^\circ$,\\
Therefore $\triangle CBE\sim \triangle FBA$,\\
Therefore $\frac{BE}{AB}=\frac{BC}{BF}$,\\
i.e., $\frac{10}{16}=\frac{6}{BF}$,\\
Therefore $BF=\boxed{\frac{48}{5}}$.
